rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal configuration with advanced components (transformer aggregation, ViT image encoder) that could yield high performance. It clarifies the effectiveness of combining complex modalities and modern architectures, which are critical design choices. This is the best use of the first experiment to set a strong baseline for subsequent comparisons.

The existing evidence shows that config_015 (transformer aggregation) achieves 0.5856 validation accuracy. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion, clarifying whether aggregation method impacts performance. It's a logical extension of the current setup, balancing exploitation (similar components) and exploration (different aggregation).

Existing evidence shows config_012 (avgpool+weighted fusion) achieves 0.635 accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion (while keeping image encoder and aggregation unchanged) could improve performance, clarifying the optimal fusion method. It balances exploitation of config_012's strong foundation with exploration of a critical design choice.

The existing evidence shows that config_012 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging transformer's ability to model complex interactions. This balances exploitation of current top performers with exploration of aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows config_012 (avgpool + weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other components identical, clarifying if the image encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on config_012's success) and exploration (testing a different image encoder).

Existing evidence shows config_002 (resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.638999). This experiment tests whether switching fusion from weighted to concat (while keeping resnet50 image encoder and avgpool aggregation) could improve performance. It clarifies the optimal fusion method for this strong image encoder setup, balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_002) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder (a more advanced encoder) with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (another strong backbone) and transformer aggregation (used in top-performing configs). It clarifies whether upgrading RNA encoder and image encoder simultaneously improves performance, balancing exploration of new components with prior success patterns.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 and resnet50 with avgpool and weighted fusion (config_002) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion, a logical extension of the current best configuration, to explore if more complex modal interactions improve performance. It balances exploitation of the promising RNA/image encoder pair with a key design choice change (aggregation method).

The existing evidence shows config_010 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests using imagenet_vit_l instead of resnet50 with the same aggregation/fusion strategy, which could reveal if the image encoder choice impacts performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about the optimal image encoder for this RNA encoder and aggregation method, offering the best chance to improve upon the current top performer with one final experiment.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (e.g., config_002) achieve moderate accuracy (0.638999), while config_022 (scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted) reaches 0.724989. This experiment tests scgpt RNA with resnet50 image and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion, a novel combination that could leverage scgpt's potential for RNA data and resnet50's image performance. It clarifies whether scgpt's modality-specific strengths can match or exceed scvi_n200's performance when paired with resnet50, balancing exploration of RNA encoders and exploitation of high-performing image encoders.
